name: Frances Ortiz
life: “I still remember trying to put back a borrowed hour hand.” People around the entrance to the Wash House know Frances by a small Friday habit. Frances stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I fixed the minute hand before I knew it wasn't minutes. I am repainting the scratches myself.
appearance: Frances is easy to recognize by a center part and straight chestnut hair and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Frances looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Frances feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To restore the scratches left by the attempted repair.
family: Harriet Ho is Frances’s cousin. Frances makes room at the table. Harriet brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *One paid trial*, Harriet says, “I wanted to announce a winner. They came back with a split-shift proposal and asked me to cost it.”
connections: Harold Pike. The keeper of harbor sounds helps confirm the repaired dial follows water again.

reactions.situation: A supervisor blames the new hire for missing the time
reactions.response: Frances checks which dial the worker saw before accepting a lateness entry.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Frances repeats the correct name quietly, making the correction easy to hear without turning it into a performance.

reactions.situation: If an argument gets loud at home
reactions.response: Frances lowers their own voice and asks for one thought at a time.
